paper_title: What are they talking about Benchmarking Large Language Models for   Knowledge-Grounded Discussion Summarization
caption: Paragraph retrieval ratios 0.90\% of LLMs. The majority of LLMs can be classified as either conservative (ratio<300.90{%}) or open retrievers (ratio>380.90{%}).
model_annotation: The bar chart displays the paragraph retrieval ratios (in percent) for a set of large language models (LLMs) evaluated in the context of knowledge-grounded discussion summarization, as referenced in the paper “Benchmarking Large Language Models for Knowledge-Grounded Discussion Summarization.” The horizontal axis lists 12 distinct LLMs — GPT-4o, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3 Opus, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama-3.1-405B, Mistral Large, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-Max, and GLM-4-Plus — arranged left to right in no apparent alphabetical or numerical order. The vertical axis, labeled “Retrieval Ratio (%)”, spans from 0 to 50 with major tick marks at intervals of 10. Each model is represented by a single vertical bar with its exact retrieval ratio value labeled above it; bar colors vary across models without an explicit legend, suggesting color is used for visual distinction rather than categorical grouping. The retrieval ratios range from a low of 25.92% (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) to a high of 46.94% (DeepSeek-V3), with most models falling between 28% and 44%. Notably, the chart includes a red annotation labeled “Expert” pointing to the GPT-4o bar, which may indicate a reference point or baseline. The caption accompanying the figure — which states that “The majority of LLMs can be classified as either conservative (ratio<300.90%) or open retrievers (ratio>380.90%)” — appears to contain a typographical error, as the values 300.90% and 380.90% are inconsistent with the chart’s 0–50% scale; the intended thresholds are likely 30.90% and 38.90%, respectively, aligning with the observed clustering of models below 30% (e.g., Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku) and above 38% (e.g., GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.1-405B, Mistral Large, DeepSeek-V3, GLM-4-Plus). No bars are visually highlighted through shading, bolding, or outlining beyond the red “Expert” annotation.

model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the paragraph retrieval ratios (expressed as percentages) for a set of large language models (LLMs) evaluated in the context of knowledge-grounded discussion summarization, as presented in the paper “Benchmarking Large Language Models for Knowledge-Grounded Discussion Summarization.” The vertical axis represents the “Retrieval Ratio (%)” ranging from 0 to 50, with tick marks at intervals of 10, while the horizontal axis lists 13 distinct LLMs: GPT-4o, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3 Opus, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama-3.1-405B, Mistral Large, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-Max, and GLM-4-Plus. Each model is represented by a uniquely colored bar with its exact retrieval ratio labeled above it. The values range from a low of 25.92% (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) to a high of 46.94% (DeepSeek-V3), with most models falling between 28% and 44%. The chart visually groups models into two broad categories as noted in the caption: “conservative retrievers” (those with ratios below 30%) — including GPT-4-turbo (29.07%), GPT-4o-mini (29.16%), and Claude 3.5 Sonnet (25.92%) — and “open retrievers” (those with ratios above 38%) — including GPT-4o (34.11% — though slightly below 38%, it is close), Claude 3 Opus (43.57%), Llama-3.1-405B (39.37%), Mistral Large (37.99% — also borderline), DeepSeek-V3 (46.94%), and GLM-4-Plus (43.58%). The caption’s thresholds (300.90% and 380.90%) appear to be typographical errors and should likely read 30.90% and 38.90% respectively, given the scale and values shown. The chart does not use sorting or special highlighting beyond color differentiation, and the term “Expert” appears in red at the bottom left, possibly indicating a reference point or baseline, though it is not quantified in the chart.
